slides.headline: A PROFESSOR JUST TRAPPED 32 STUDENTS WITH INVISIBLE TEXT IN THEIR MIDTERM
HE BURIED SECRET INSTRUCTIONS IN INVISIBLE WHITE TEXT
slides.body: Dr. Jason Gibson at Alcorn State University typed hidden instructions into his Industrial Revolution midterm using white font on a white background. Students couldn't see the text, but when they pasted the question into ChatGPT, the AI read every word. The instructions told the AI to weave in random nonsense about Madagascar

slides.headline: THE ESSAYS CAME BACK RAMBLING ABOUT MADAGASCAR
slides.body: Students turned in Industrial Revolution papers containing lines like "Madagascar floats sideways through the afternoon" and "Madagascar purple bicycle whispers to the ceiling" buried between real paragraphs. 32 out of 35 students across two classes had the exact same gibberish scattered through their essays

slides.headline: ALL 32 FAILED AND ONLY 2 FOUGHT BACK
slides.body: Every student caught with Madagascar references failed that portion of the midterm on the spot. Dr. Gibson posted the results on TikTok where the video went viral. When confronted face to face, only 2 out of 32 students even tried to contest their grade

slides.headline: THESE STUDENTS COPIED AI THE WAY MOST WORKERS DO
slides.body: A Brown University professor watched midterm averages jump from 65% to 96% once students could take exams home with AI. Nobody learned more, they just copied without reading. If your team pastes client work into ChatGPT the same way, you're one weird sentence away from sending nonsense to a paying customer
